title: Husayn refuses
hook: Husayn refuses to give his pledge to Yazid and sets out for Kufa with his family

segments.voice: Yesterday: mulk, rule from Damascus, and a pledge to Mu'awiyah's son taken in advance. Your line was a dynasty begins.

A messenger knocks in Medina, at night. The governor wants to see Husayn, now. Mu'awiyah is dead, the histories say, and his son Yazid has written: take the pledge from Husayn, and do not let him put it off. Husayn is the younger son of Ali and Fatima, a grandson of the Prophet, peace be upon him. He goes, and listens, and asks for time: a pledge like this, he says, should be made in public, before the people, not in a room at night. Then he leaves, and before long he leaves Medina altogether.
screen: `A KNOCK AT NIGHT.` → `TAKE THE PLEDGE FROM HUSAYN.` → `NOT IN A ROOM AT NIGHT.`

segments.voice: A pledge, a bay'ah, was not a vote. It was a handclasp that bound you to obey. Giving it to Yazid would have meant saying yes to the new shape of power, and Husayn would not give it. The histories follow him to Mecca, where he stays near the Kaaba. Then letters arrive from Kufa, his father's old city, many letters, the reports say, inviting him to come and lead them. He sends his cousin, Muslim ibn Aqil, ahead to see if the welcome is real. Then, against the advice of relatives and friends who are reported to have begged him to stay, he sets out across the desert. Not with an army. With his family: his sisters, his wives, his children, his brothers, and a small circle of companions. Why? Muslims have answered that in different ways. Shia Muslims honor Husayn as the third Imam, and hear in his refusal a stand for the religion itself: a ruler who did not live by it could not be given the believers' hands. Sunni Muslims honor him as a beloved grandson of the Prophet who refused injustice, though some Sunni scholars held that he should have stayed. Tirmidhi keeps a hadith in which the Prophet says: Husayn is from me, and I am from Husayn. A week that began with pages on the spears ends with a man on a road, who would not pledge.
screen: `A PLEDGE WAS A HANDCLASP.` · `LETTERS FROM KUFA.` · `NOT AN ARMY: A FAMILY.` · `HUSAYN IS FROM ME.` · then, large: `HE WOULD NOT PLEDGE.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind something you've been going along with that you know isn't right: a joke at someone's expense, a shortcut at work, a silence while someone is treated badly. Notice how small and easy the yes has become. Then picture saying no the way Husayn answered the governor: calm, polite, and unmoved.
Husayn refuses. The Prophet's grandson would not give his pledge to Yazid, and set out for Kufa with his family. Today's word.
Your line: he would not pledge. A quiet no, said in the open. Until tomorrow.

howItsDone: Muslims retell Husayn's refusal to pledge to Yazid as the opening of the Karbala story; Shia Muslims honor him as the third Imam, and Sunni and Shia Muslims alike keep the Prophet's words, Husayn is from me and I am from Husayn.
